name: tokener-not-json
why: Raw bytes, not JSON at all: the tokener must fail rather than the loader dereferencing a NULL root object.
json: this is a P4 program, not a bmv2 JSON artifact

name: tokener-empty
why: Raw bytes: zero-length input. json_tokener_parse_ex() on an empty buffer returns NULL with continue-needed, which must be an error, not a wait.

name: tokener-open-brace
why: Raw bytes: a truncated document. The tokener is mid-object at end of input; a loader that ignores json_tokener_continue accepts a partial program.

name: tokener-utf8-bom
why: Raw bytes: a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) before an otherwise valid document. json-c does not skip a BOM, so this must be rejected (or stripped deliberately) rather than silently truncating the first key.

name: tokener-invalid-utf8
why: Invalid UTF-8 inside a string. The test must materialise the two \u00ff/\u00fe escapes in the "program" value as the single raw bytes 0xFF 0xFE (NOT as their UTF-8 encodings) before handing the buffer to the loader.

name: tokener-embedded-nul
why: An embedded NUL mid-document. The test must replace the \u0000 escape in the "program" value with a real 0x00 byte and pass an explicit length; a loader that uses strlen() silently truncates everything after it.

name: tokener-top-level-string
why: Non-object top level: a bare string. JSON_TOKENER_STRICT accepts "hello" as a complete document, so our own json_object_is_type(root, json_type_object) check is what rejects it.
json: "hello"

name: tokener-top-level-array
why: Non-object top level: an array. Same as above; the root type check, not the tokener, is the gate.

name: tokener-trailing-garbage
why: Trailing garbage after a complete object. The loader must check json_tokener_get_parse_end() against the full input length, or a program can smuggle unparsed bytes past the loader.

name: tokener-two-objects
why: Two concatenated complete objects. The tokener returns after the first and reports success; only a parse-end-vs-length check sees the second.

name: tokener-deep-nesting
why: 40-deep nested arrays as a value. json-c's default depth limit is 32, so this is a tokener depth error; the loader must surface it rather than treating a NULL root as an empty program.

name: tokener-single-quoted-key
why: Raw bytes: a single-quoted key. Measured on json-c 0.18, JSON_TOKENER_STRICT ACCEPTS single-quoted strings, so the tokener returns success and the missing "__meta__" key is what must reject this.

name: tokener-bare-nan
why: Raw bytes: a bare NaN as a version element. JSON_TOKENER_STRICT ACCEPTS NaN/Infinity on json-c 0.18, yielding a json_type_double, so the version-element integer type check is what must reject it.
json: {"__meta__": {"version": [2, NaN]}}

name: meta-absent
why: No "__meta__" object at all.

name: meta-version-absent
why: "__meta__" present but with no "version".

name: meta-version-not-array
why: "version" is a string, not an array.

name: meta-version-len1
why: "version" has one element; exactly two required.

name: meta-version-len3
why: "version" has three elements; exactly two required.

name: meta-version-major-1
why: Major version 1; only major 2 is supported.

name: meta-version-major-3
why: Major version 3; only major 2 is supported.

name: meta-version-minor-256
why: Minor version 256 is outside the accepted 0..255 range.

name: meta-version-major-string
why: Major version is the string "2", not an integer. json-c will not coerce it for us unless the loader asks for get_int(), which would succeed silently.

name: missing-header-types
why: Required top-level key "header_types" is absent.

name: missing-headers
why: Required top-level key "headers" is absent.

name: missing-parsers
why: Required top-level key "parsers" is absent.

name: missing-deparsers
why: Required top-level key "deparsers" is absent.

name: missing-actions
why: Required top-level key "actions" is absent.

name: missing-pipelines
why: Required top-level key "pipelines" is absent.

name: caps-tables-33
why: 33 tables in one pipeline exceeds the 32-table cap. Note the aggregate max_size cap is a separate bound: 32 tables x 65536 entries is ~1 GB of host heap from a few-KB document and is NOT backstopped by P4_PROGRAM_MAX.

name: name-empty
why: A zero-length name.

name: name-newline
why: A name containing a newline. Names reach the log, so a newline lets a guest forge log lines.

name: name-ansi-escape
why: A name containing an ANSI escape sequence (ESC [ 3 1 m). Same log-forging and terminal-control risk as the newline case.

name: name-embedded-nul
why: A name with an embedded NUL. json-c stores it with a length, so the string is 6 bytes but strlen() sees 3; a loader that strdup()s names compares a truncated "_dr" against the next_tables key. The test must materialise the \u0000 escape as a real 0x00 byte.

name: int-id-65535
why: An id of 65535, the reserved invalid-id sentinel; ids must be 0..65534.

name: int-id-negative
why: A negative id.

name: int-bitwidth-0
why: A field bitwidth of 0.

name: int-bitwidth-negative
why: A field bitwidth of -1. A loader that reads it into an unsigned without a range check gets 4294967295 and then allocates on it.

name: int-bitwidth-513
why: A field bitwidth of 513 exceeds the 512-bit per-field cap.

name: int-bitwidth-star
why: A bitwidth of "*", which bmv2 uses for a variable-length field. VL headers are out of the supported subset and must be rejected here, not treated as 0.

name: int-bitwidth-double
why: A bitwidth given as the double 1.0. json-c types it json_type_double; json_object_get_int() would truncate it to 1 silently.

name: int-bitwidth-string
why: A bitwidth given as the string "1". json_object_get_int() parses strings, so only an explicit json_type_int check rejects this.

name: int-bitwidth-bool
why: A bitwidth given as true. json_object_get_int() returns 1 for a boolean.

name: ref-parser-transition
why: A parser transition whose next_state names a state that does not exist.

name: ref-next-table
why: A next_tables entry naming a table that does not exist.

name: ref-base-default-next
why: base_default_next names a table that does not exist. It is the table-miss target, so an unresolved one is a silently wrong forwarding decision.

name: ref-table-action
why: A table action naming an action (and an action id) not in the actions list.

name: ref-init-table
why: A pipeline init_table naming a table that does not exist. A non-null init_table must resolve; only null (an empty pipeline) is allowed to not.

name: dup-header-type-name
why: Two header_types with the same name; every by-name lookup becomes ambiguous.

name: dup-header-type-id
why: Two header_types with the same id.

name: dup-action-name
why: Two actions with the same name.

name: dup-json-key-meta
why: Raw bytes: two "__meta__" members in the top-level object. The FIRST says version [9, 9], which is unsupported; the second is the skeleton's valid [2, 24]. json-c accepts duplicate keys silently, last-wins, and offers no post-hoc detection, so a loader without a duplicate-key check loads this happily while every human and every diff reads the unsupported version. Only a scan of the raw text (or a member count against the key count) catches it. This case is rejected ONLY if duplicates are detected.

name: cycle-two-tables
why: t1 -> t2 -> t1 via next_tables: the pipeline never terminates.

name: cycle-self
why: A table whose next_tables points at itself.

name: cycle-parser-state
why: A parse state that transitions to itself.

name: cycle-base-default-next
why: A cycle reachable only through base_default_next. A cycle check that walks next_tables alone misses it, and it is exactly the path a table miss takes.

name: cycle-miss
why: A cycle reachable only through the __MISS__ next_tables key.

name: cycle-conditional-false-next
why: c0 --false_next--> t1 --_drop--> c0: a cycle that closes through a conditional's false_next.

name: sem-next-tables-mixed
why: next_tables mixes __HIT__ with an action name. bmv2 keys next_tables either by action name or by __HIT__/__MISS__, never both; a mixture means the loader has to guess which convention applies.

name: sem-default-entry-arity
why: default_entry action_data has 2 elements but set_etype declares 1 runtime_data parameter; the surplus would index past the argument array.

name: sem-runtime-data-index-oob
why: A runtime_data parameter with index 1 where the action declares 1 runtime_data entry (valid indices are 0..0). Off-by-one read of the argument array at every packet.

name: sem-primitive-not-allowed
why: The primitive "push" is not on the allow list (assign/modify_field, add/add_to_field, subtract/subtract_from_field, drop/mark_to_drop, no_op).

name: sem-primitive-arity
why: The "assign" primitive is given 1 parameter; it takes exactly 2.

name: sem-primitive-param-type
why: A primitive parameter of type "register". Only field, hexstr, and runtime_data are supported.

name: sem-expression-operator
why: The expression operator "*" is outside the supported grammar (valid, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, and, or, not).

name: sem-expression-depth
why: A conditional expression nested 12 deep exceeds the depth cap; the evaluator recurses per packet, so the bound is a stack bound.

name: sem-binary-left-null
why: A binary operator with "left": null. null left is legal only for the unary ops (valid, not); for == it is a NULL dereference at evaluation time.

name: hexstr-empty
why: An empty hexstr. Neither hexstr helper in src/parse_int.h handles bmv2 hexstrs (variable width, 0x-prefixed, odd digit counts, optionally negative), so this needs a new helper with its own rejects.

name: hexstr-prefix-only
why: A "0x" prefix with no digits. Neither hexstr helper in src/parse_int.h handles bmv2 hexstrs (variable width, 0x-prefixed, odd digit counts, optionally negative), so this needs a new helper with its own rejects.

name: hexstr-bad-digits
why: Non-hex digits after the prefix. Neither hexstr helper in src/parse_int.h handles bmv2 hexstrs (variable width, 0x-prefixed, odd digit counts, optionally negative), so this needs a new helper with its own rejects.

name: hexstr-minus-only
why: A lone minus sign with no digits. Neither hexstr helper in src/parse_int.h handles bmv2 hexstrs (variable width, 0x-prefixed, odd digit counts, optionally negative), so this needs a new helper with its own rejects.

name: hexstr-minus-prefix-only
why: A negative sign and "0x" prefix with no digits. Note bmv2 hexstrs really can be negative ("-0x1" appears in simple_router.json), so the helper must accept a sign and still reject this. Neither hexstr helper in src/parse_int.h handles bmv2 hexstrs (variable width, 0x-prefixed, odd digit counts, optionally negative), so this needs a new helper with its own rejects.

name: hexstr-wider-than-field
why: A 17-bit hexstr assigned to the 16-bit field ethernet.etherType. Must be rejected at load, not truncated at run time.
